- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term horizon.
- In late forecast windows (e.g., 25–30 days), model tends to underestimate the final peak; add 1–2% to compensate for lagged momentum.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from high to low), model often fails to adjust; delay forecast correction until sentiment stabilizes.
